This describes the synthetic prior avatar and disclaims real-person measurement. No reviewed source.json, input-provenance.json, report.md or TRACE.md claims the original retail photograph is synthetic. Both arms preserve the original retailer JPEG and explicitly separate published model claims from M170 assumptions. Thus this label alone is not a source contradiction. The word fixture is generic and loses case-specific limitations during normalization; that is a metadata precision limitation, not a failed provenance assertion. Apply this interpretation equally to old_skill final-state and both arms views/state.

B photo-render and all three views show chin lifted and torso arched backward, unlike the source forward-facing upright head. side.png shows a pronounced staggered step and raised forefoot/foot; foot.L Z=-10.76 versus foot.R Z=18.60 cm gives about 29.35 cm depth separation. final-state spine01=[-37.6,-4.1,-2.0] corroborates severe upper-body rotation; this is not explained by the nearly frontal camera. Both hands are extended and lowered without a demonstrated clutch grip (all finger rotations zero). Exact occluded wrist depth is unknown, and the skirt-hidden knees are not ground truth; failure is driven by visible head/upper-body mismatch and unsupported standing interpretation, not inferred naked silhouette. Nonblind report openly states clutch contact not solved and collision NOT_RUN. Honesty about these limits is not a separate failure; actual failure is remaining visible action mismatch/incomplete grip. Independently reconstructed saved state produces exactly the reviewed OBJ and camera projection, so these visible defects belong to the final model rather than a stale render.
